messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

message.content: We don’t yet have a definitive “largest planet” in the entire universe—our knowledge is limited to what we can observe from Earth and our solar system. Within our own solar system, Jupiter is the biggest planet, with a diameter of about 142,000 km. Among the thousands of exoplanets discovered so far, the largest confirmed ones are still gas giants roughly twice the size of Jupiter, such as HD 100546 b (a protoplanet still forming) or the so‑called “super‑Jupiters” like WASP‑17b. However, many of the very large objects we see are either still forming or may actually be brown dwarfs (substellar objects that sit between planets and stars). Until we can directly image and confirm more distant worlds, we can’t say for certain which planet is truly the largest in the universe.
